document_title: The tax break came first. Saronic's Brownsville shipyard
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
The county decided before Saronic did.

The Texas Tribune reported on June 18th that the Cameron County Commissioners Court approved a $211 million tax break for Saronic. The court hoped the company would pick the Port of Brownsville. Opponents told the court it would take money from public schools.

That month Saronic told the Tribune it had not yet chosen a site.

The Tribune reported a 95% abatement over 20 years. It would require 35% of the full-time workforce to be local. The break would shrink if Saronic fell short of job projections.

On September 30th Saronic broke ground in Brownsville. It calls Port Alpha a software-defined yard for autonomous and manned ships. It puts private capital at more than $3 billion and direct jobs at up to 10,000.

Up to 10,000 is Saronic's own figure. Who will count the jobs, and when?

#CameronCounty #PortOfBrownsville #Saronic

S1.body: Saronic broke ground on Port Alpha, a shipyard for autonomous and manned ships, at the Port of Brownsville on September 30th. The Tribune reported the county approved its tax break in June, before Saronic had picked the port. The vessel is drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: An autonomous boat made a rescue, Saronic says
S2.body: Its home page claims the first known at-sea rescue by an autonomous boat. The deckhouse and mast are drawn to illustrate, not Saronic's design.

S4.headline: 835 acres, and an option on more
S4.body: Port Alpha sits on 835 acres, with an option to expand to nearly 4,400, Saronic says. Each is drawn as a square of that area, not the site's real shape.
